subproblem.title: A real sequence converges if a(q(i)) − a(p(i)) → 0 for all pairs of index maps p, q → ∞ (real-analysis part of supplied Step 6)
subproblem.statement: Let a : ℕ → ℝ. Assume that for all maps p, q : ℕ → ℕ with p(i) → ∞ and q(i) → ∞ as i → ∞ (Tendsto p atTop atTop and Tendsto q atTop atTop), a(q(i)) − a(p(i)) → 0 as i → ∞. Then a converges: there is s ∈ ℝ with a(n) → s as n → ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ p q : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto p atTop atTop → Tendsto q atTop atTop → Tendsto (fun i => a (q i) - a (p i)) atTop (𝓝 0)) → ∃ s : ℝ, Tendsto a atTop (𝓝 s)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the Cauchy argument at the end of Step 6 of the parent proof, stated for an arbitrary real sequence. The parent text reads: '(a_n) is a Cauchy sequence: otherwise there is ε > 0 such that for every i there are p(i), q(i) ≥ i with |a_{q(i)} − a_{p(i)}| ≥ ε; then p and q tend to ∞ while a_{q(i)} − a_{p(i)} does not tend to 0, contradicting the claim. Since ℝ is complete, (a_n) converges.' The parent applies it to a_n := X(η_n(ω)); the hypothesis is the claim of Step 6, which (CL) supplies for the reindexed approximations (G_{p(i)})_i and (G_{q(i)})_i.

1. (Cauchy criterion.) We show that a is a Cauchy sequence. By Metric.cauchySeq_iff, this means: for every ε > 0 there is N such that dist(a_i, a_j) = |a_i − a_j| < ε for all i, j ≥ N. Suppose not. Then there is ε > 0 such that for every N ∈ ℕ there are i, j ≥ N with |a_i − a_j| ≥ ε.
2. (Index maps.) By choice, pick for every N ∈ ℕ such indices p(N) ≥ N and q(N) ≥ N, so |a_{p(N)} − a_{q(N)}| ≥ ε. The identity map tends to ∞ and p(N) ≥ N, q(N) ≥ N for all N, so p and q tend to ∞ (tendsto_atTop_mono).
3. (Contradiction.) By the hypothesis applied to p and q, a(q(i)) − a(p(i)) → 0. By Metric.tendsto_nhds, eventually |a(q(i)) − a(p(i)) − 0| < ε; take one such i. Then |a_{p(i)} − a_{q(i)}| = |a_{q(i)} − a_{p(i)}| < ε. This contradicts |a_{p(i)} − a_{q(i)}| ≥ ε from step 2. Hence a is Cauchy.
4. (Completeness.) ℝ is complete, so the Cauchy sequence a converges to some s ∈ ℝ (cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete). ∎
proof_key_steps: If a is not Cauchy, there are ε > 0 and, for every N, indices p(N), q(N) ≥ N with |a_{p(N)} − a_{q(N)}| ≥ ε.
Since p(N), q(N) ≥ N, both p and q tend to ∞, so the hypothesis gives a(q(i)) − a(p(i)) → 0, which contradicts the ε-gap at some i.
ℝ is complete, so the Cauchy sequence a converges.

audit.reason: The exact proposition requires arbitrary index maps tending to infinity. Failure of the Cauchy criterion supplies p(N), q(N) ≥ N; the assumed difference convergence contradicts their fixed positive separation. Completeness then gives the limit. This is an independent obligation used directly in parent step 6.

subproblem.title: The support of a current characterized by compatible approximations G_n → G lies in closure(G(spt X)) (supplied Step 11)
subproblem.statement: Notation: ℝ^p := Eucl p; D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q and D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q; spt = support; for a covector γ and a continuous linear map T, γ∘T := γ.compContinuousLinearMap T. Let m, m′, k ∈ ℕ, X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m), S ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}) and G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, and let G_n : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} (n ∈ ℕ) be continuous maps with G_n → G uniformly on spt X. Assume that for every ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) and every sequence (η_n) in D^k(ℝ^m) such that, for all sufficiently large n, there is an open N ⊆ ℝ^m with spt X ⊆ N and η_n(x) = ω(G_n(x))∘(fderiv ℝ G_n x) for all x ∈ N, the sequence X(η_n) converges to S(ω). Then spt S ⊆ closure(G(spt X)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m m' k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl m)) k) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl m')) k) (G : Eucl m → Eucl m') (Gj : ℕ → Eucl m → Eucl m'), (∀ n, Continuous (Gj n)) → TendstoUniformlyOn Gj G atTop X.support → (∀ (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl m')) k) (ηj : ℕ → TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl m)) k), (∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ N : Set (Eucl m), IsOpen N ∧ X.support ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, (ηj n : DifferentialForm (Eucl m) k) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl m') k) (Gj n x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ (Gj n) x)) → Tendsto (fun n => X (ηj n)) atTop (𝓝 (S ω))) → S.support ⊆ closure (G '' X.support)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 11 of the parent proof. There the hypothesis is the characterization LipPF(X, G, S) of Step 9, applied to the reference sequence: the maps G_n are C^∞, hence continuous, and converge to G uniformly on (spt X)_{r/2} ⊇ spt X, hence on spt X. Recall the definitions. S vanishes on W (S.VanishesOn W) if S(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. zeroRegion(S) is the union of all open W ⊆ ℝ^{m′} with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ univ and S vanishing on W. spt S = univ ∖ zeroRegion(S).

1. (Setup.) Let y₀ ∈ spt S. Suppose, for contradiction, that y₀ ∉ closure(G(spt X)). The complement of the closed set closure(G(spt X)) is open and contains y₀, so there is ε > 0 with ball(y₀, ε) ∩ closure(G(spt X)) = ∅ (Metric.isOpen_iff). Put ρ := ε/3 > 0. For every x ∈ spt X, G(x) ∈ G(spt X) ⊆ closure(G(spt X)), so G(x) ∉ ball(y₀, ε), i.e. dist(G(x), y₀) ≥ ε.
2. (S vanishes on W := ball(y₀, ρ).) Let ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
   (a) By uniform convergence on spt X (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff), for all sufficiently large n: dist(G(x), G_n(x)) < ρ for every x ∈ spt X.
   (b) Fix such an n and put N_n := G_n⁻¹(ℝ^{m′} ∖ tsupport ω). It is open: it is the preimage, under the continuous map G_n, of the open complement of the closed set tsupport ω.
   (c) spt X ⊆ N_n. Let x ∈ spt X and suppose G_n(x) ∈ tsupport ω. Then G_n(x) ∈ W, i.e. dist(G_n(x), y₀) < ρ. By step 1 and the triangle inequality, ε ≤ dist(G(x), y₀) ≤ dist(G(x), G_n(x)) + dist(G_n(x), y₀) < ρ + ρ = 2ε/3 < ε, a contradiction. So G_n(x) ∉ tsupport ω, i.e. x ∈ N_n.
   (d) Let x ∈ N_n. Then G_n(x) ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(G_n(x)) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). Hence ω(G_n(x))∘(fderiv ℝ G_n x) = 0, since the pull-back of the zero covector is zero. This is the value at x of the zero form 0 ∈ D^k(ℝ^m).
   (e) By (a)–(d), for all sufficiently large n the constant sequence η_n := 0 satisfies the compatibility condition of the hypothesis for ω, with N := N_n. Hence X(0) → S(ω). But X is linear, so X(0) = 0 for every n, and the constant sequence 0 converges to 0. Limits in ℝ are unique (tendsto_nhds_unique), so S(ω) = 0.
   As ω was arbitrary, S vanishes on W.
3. (y₀ ∈ zeroRegion(S).) W = ball(y₀, ρ) is open. Its closure lies in closedBall(y₀, ρ) (closure_ball_subset_closedBall), which is compact because ℝ^{m′} is proper (isCompact_closedBall). So closure W is compact, as a closed subset of a compact set, and closure W ⊆ univ. With step 2, W belongs to the family whose union is zeroRegion(S). Since ρ > 0, y₀ ∈ W, hence y₀ ∈ zeroRegion(S).
4. (Conclusion.) spt S = univ ∖ zeroRegion(S), so y₀ ∉ spt S, which contradicts step 1. Hence every point of spt S lies in closure(G(spt X)), i.e. spt S ⊆ closure(G(spt X)). ∎
proof_key_steps: A point y₀ ∉ closure(G(spt X)) has a ball of radius ε = 3ρ disjoint from that closure, so dist(G(x), y₀) ≥ 3ρ for x ∈ spt X.

Let ω be supported in ball(y₀, ρ), and let n be large enough that dist(G, G_n) < ρ on spt X. Then G_n(x) ∉ tsupport ω on the open set N_n := G_n⁻¹(ℝ^{m′} ∖ tsupport ω) ⊇ spt X, so the zero form is compatible with (G_n, ω).
The hypothesis then gives X(0) = 0 → S(ω), so S(ω) = 0, and S vanishes on ball(y₀, ρ).
That ball is open with compact closure, so y₀ ∈ zeroRegion(S), i.e. y₀ ∉ spt S.

audit.reason: The proof establishes the exact statement using only continuity and uniform convergence on support. Separation from the closed image makes the zero forms eventually compatible; the characterization forces S to vanish on a ball with compact closure. The definition of zeroRegion then yields the support inclusion. No differentiability assumption or circular appeal to the parent is needed.

subproblem.title: Bounded compatible pull-back forms for a C^∞ map that is proper on A and has ‖Df‖ ≤ Λ on an open O ⊇ A (supplied Steps 2–3)
subproblem.statement: Notation: ℝ^p := Eucl p; D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q; |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ; for a covector γ on ℝ^{m′} and a continuous linear map T : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, γ∘T := γ.compContinuousLinearMap T; C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞). Let m, m′, k ∈ ℕ, let f : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} be C^∞, let A ⊆ O ⊆ ℝ^m with O open, and let Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 with ‖fderiv ℝ f x‖ ≤ Λ for every x ∈ O. Assume that f is proper on A: f⁻¹(K) ∩ A is compact for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^{m′}. Then for every ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) there is η ∈ D^k(ℝ^m) such that (i) η is compatible with (f, ω) near A: there is an open N ⊆ ℝ^m with A ⊆ N and η(x) = ω(f(x))∘(fderiv ℝ f x) for every x ∈ N; and (ii) for every C ∈ ℝ with |ω(y)| ≤ C for all y ∈ ℝ^{m′}, one has |η(x)| ≤ Λ^k·C for all x ∈ ℝ^m.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m m' k : ℕ) (f : Eucl m → Eucl m') (A O : Set (Eucl m)) (Λ : ℝ≥0), IsOpen O → A ⊆ O → ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f → (∀ x ∈ O, ‖fderiv ℝ f x‖ ≤ Λ) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl m'), IsCompact K → IsCompact (f ⁻¹' K ∩ A)) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl m')) k, ∃ η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl m)) k, (∃ N : Set (Eucl m), IsOpen N ∧ A ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl m) k) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl m') k) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∧ ∀ C : ℝ, (∀ y, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl m') k) y) ≤ C) → ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((η : DifferentialForm (Eucl m) k) x) ≤ (Λ : ℝ) ^ k * C
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 2 and 3 of the parent proof (homogeneity of |·|; compatible forms with bounds), stated for one C^∞ map f that is proper on a set A and has ‖Df‖ ≤ Λ on an open O ⊇ A. The parent applies it for n ≥ n₀ with f := G_n, A := spt X and O := O₀ = (spt X)_{r/2}, and puts η_n(ω) := 0 for n < n₀. Notation as in the statement; Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x. Recall that TestFormOn U k consists of the differential k-forms that are C^∞, have compact support, and satisfy tsupport ⊆ U.

1. (Compatible form; reused compatible_form.) Apply iwl_sp_exists_compatible_testForm with P := m, Q := m′, j := k, U := O, V := univ, the set A and the map f. Its hypotheses hold: O is open, A ⊆ O, f is C^∞, and for every compact K ⊆ univ the set f⁻¹(K) ∩ A is compact by the properness hypothesis. Applied to ω ∈ TestFormOn univ k, it gives η₀ ∈ TestFormOn O k, ζ : ℝ^m → ℝ and N ⊆ ℝ^m such that N is open, A ⊆ N, 0 ≤ ζ(x) ≤ 1 for all x, η₀(x) = ζ(x)·(ω(f x)∘Df(x)) for all x, and η₀(x) = ω(f x)∘Df(x) for all x ∈ N. Its last conclusion (tsupport η₀ ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω)) is not needed.
2. (Change of domain.) η₀ is C^∞ and has compact support because η₀ ∈ TestFormOn O k, and tsupport η₀ ⊆ univ holds trivially. So the same differential form is an element η of TestFormOn univ k = D^k(ℝ^m), with η(x) = η₀(x) for every x. By step 1, η(x) = ω(f x)∘Df(x) for every x ∈ N, where N is open and A ⊆ N. This is (i).
3. (Homogeneity of |·|.) For c ∈ ℝ and a k-covector γ on ℝ^m: |c·γ| = |c|·|γ|. By definition |γ| = √Σ_I [I strictly increasing] γ(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(k)})², summed over I : Fin k → Fin m, where e is the standard basis. Since (c·γ)(v) = c·γ(v), every term of the sum for c·γ is c² times the corresponding term for γ, so that sum equals c²·Σ (Finset.mul_sum). Hence |c·γ| = √(c²·Σ) = √(c²)·√Σ = |c|·|γ| (Real.sqrt_mul with c² ≥ 0, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).
4. (Bound.) Let C ∈ ℝ with |ω(y)| ≤ C for all y. Then C ≥ |ω(0)| ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg), so Λ^k·C ≥ 0. Fix x ∈ ℝ^m.
   (a) Case x ∈ O. By steps 1–3 and ζ(x) ≥ 0: |η(x)| = |ζ(x)·(ω(f x)∘Df(x))| = ζ(x)·|ω(f x)∘Df(x)|. Since ζ(x) ≤ 1 and |·| ≥ 0, this is at most |ω(f x)∘Df(x)|. The reused pullback_norm (iwl_sp_covectorEuclideanNorm_pullback_le with P := m, Q := m′, j := k, L := Df(x), α := ω(f x)) gives |ω(f x)∘Df(x)| ≤ ‖Df(x)‖^k·|ω(f x)|. By hypothesis 0 ≤ ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ Λ, because x ∈ O, so ‖Df(x)‖^k ≤ Λ^k (u ↦ u^k is monotone on [0, ∞); pow_le_pow_left₀). Together with 0 ≤ |ω(f x)| ≤ C and Λ^k ≥ 0 this gives ‖Df(x)‖^k·|ω(f x)| ≤ Λ^k·C. Hence |η(x)| ≤ Λ^k·C.
   (b) Case x ∉ O. Since η₀ ∈ TestFormOn O k, tsupport η₀ ⊆ O, so x ∉ tsupport η₀. Hence η(x) = η₀(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and |η(x)| = |0| = 0 ≤ Λ^k·C (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero).
   This proves (ii) for every x.
5. (Conclusion.) η ∈ D^k(ℝ^m) satisfies (i) by step 2 and (ii) by step 4. ∎
proof_key_steps: Write f^#ω for the pull-back x ↦ ω(f x)∘Df(x). compatible_form with U := O and V := univ gives η₀ ∈ D^k(O), ζ with values in [0, 1], and an open N ⊇ A such that η₀ = ζ·f^#ω everywhere and η₀ = f^#ω on N.
tsupport η₀ ⊆ O ⊆ univ, so η₀ is an element η of D^k(ℝ^m), compatible with (f, ω) on N.
|c·γ| = |c|·|γ| for the coefficient norm, because the sum of squares scales by c².
On O: |η(x)| = ζ(x)|f^#ω(x)| ≤ ‖Df(x)‖^k|ω(f x)| ≤ Λ^k·C by pullback_norm. Off O: η(x) = 0 because tsupport η₀ ⊆ O.
